summary: This resolution sets special floor procedures for immediate House consideration of H.R. 1908 (the End Congressional Stock Trading Act), waiving points of order, automatically adopting a substitute amendment that bars Members of Congress and their immediate families from owning or trading most stocks, bonds, commodities, and complex investments (with limited exceptions and phased divestment deadlines), limiting debate to one hour, and allowing only a motion to recommit before final passage.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a procedural resolution to consider legislation banning congressional stock ownership and trading. It contains no provisions related to government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.

Section 2(e) of the underlying bill amends IRC section 1043 to allow nonrecognition of capital gains on required divestitures of securities. This provides a targeted tax benefit (deferral of gains tax) to Members of Congress and their families complying with the divestment mandate, constituting a narrow form of tax relief.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, providers, or public health programs.
No provisions address firearms, gun ownership, or related regulations.
No provisions address immigration, visas, borders, or related enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions address military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy.
No provisions address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance policy.
The bill creates civil penalties for violations but does not engage broader criminal justice reform, sentencing, or policing issues.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or campaign finance beyond a narrow prohibition on using campaign funds to pay civil penalties.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address workers' rights, unions, or employment policy.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
